title: An ordinary Monday
hook: At a well, on an errand, Jesus says worship needs neither this mountain nor Jerusalem
tomorrow: what did the Buddha remember about sitting in the shade as a boy?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Thoreau at the end: no quarrel, a peace that grew out of ordinary days. Now the ordinary days themselves, starting with a Monday.

Retreat photos are mostly mountains: a yoga deck above the clouds, a monastery on a cliff. Then the alarm goes off on Monday. John's Gospel has a story for that gap. Jesus, tired from the road, sits down by a well. A Samaritan woman comes out to draw water, an ordinary errand on an ordinary day, and he asks her for a drink. Their talk turns to an old argument between their peoples. Her ancestors worshiped on this mountain, she says, and his people say Jerusalem. So which mountain is it?
screen: `RETREATS ARE MOUNTAINS.` → `A WELL, AN ERRAND.` → `THIS MOUNTAIN OR JERUSALEM?`

segments.voice: Jesus answers: "Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father." Then he says where: "the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth." Christians take this as a teaching about place: God isn't kept on one mountain. God is met in spirit and in truth, which can happen at a well with a water jar. Here's a neighbor who says something close. In the Chan Buddhist tradition of China, Layman Pang, a householder and not a monk, wrote that his miraculous power and wondrous activity was drawing water and carrying firewood. What they share: the holy found in the plainest chore, even the same water. An honest difference: Jesus speaks of worshiping the Father, a God who seeks people out; Layman Pang names no God, and the wonder is the chore itself. Neither one needs a mountain. That's what this path carries into the ordinary days. A practice that only works on retreat isn't finished yet. Monday is where it's tested: your rule, done plainly, on a day when nothing happens.
screen: `NEITHER THIS MOUNTAIN NOR JERUSALEM.` · `IN SPIRIT AND IN TRUTH.` · `LAYMAN PANG: DRAWING WATER.` · `MONDAY IS THE TEST.` · then, large: `PLAIN DAYS.`

segments.voice: Listen to one ordinary sound around you: a fridge humming, traffic, a door down the hall. For the rest of the sit, let that plain sound be the place, and each time your mind goes looking for somewhere better, come back to it.
An ordinary Monday: a plain day, which, in the story at the well, is place enough. Worship needs no mountain.
The line to keep: plain days, a well and a water jar, no mountain. Day one of fourteen ordinary ones.

howItsDone: Christians read Jesus' words at the well as worship not bound to one holy place; Chan Buddhists point to Layman Pang's water and firewood. People on this path keep their rule on plain days, not only on retreat.

Samaritan.meaning: from Samaria, a people who shared Israel's roots but worshiped apart

Jerusalem.meaning: the city of the Temple, where Jesus' people worshiped

Chan.meaning: the Chinese school of Buddhism called Zen in Japan

Layman Pang.meaning: a Chan Buddhist householder of China, known for plain wisdom
